Fe–Y2O3 nanocomposite powders with different Y2O3 contents were prepared by solution combustion synthesis and subsequent hydrogen reduction
the as-synthesized product was carried out in a tube furnace at 400°C for 2 h under flowing hydrogen, forming the Fe–Y2O3 nanocomposite powders resulted
The synthesized Fe–Y2O3 nanocomposite powders were uniaxial compaction to prepare the green compacts with a diameter of 15 mm by using a steel die under 300 MPa pressure holding for 2 min.
The green compacts were then treated at 600°C for 2 h in a tube furnace under flowing hydrogen atmosphere with a gas flow of 1 L/min.
The treated compacts were put into carbide molds at 600, 650, 700, and 800°C for SPS in vacuum atmosphere with the sintering pressure of 50 MPa for 5 min and the heating rate of 100°C/min.
